# Google Is Quietly Connecting Gemini to More of the Tools You Already Use

> **In short:** Google is pushing Gemini deeper into Workspace: upgraded AI voiceovers and customizable captions in Google Vids, new "skills" that replace Gems, comment APIs for Docs/Sheets/Slides, easier client-side encryption, and a new connectors path that ties Gemini to CRMs, project tools, and more apps via Zapier.

If you've ever bounced between Gmail, a CRM, a project tracker, and a video editor just to finish one task, you know how messy "all your work in one place" usually gets. Google says it's chipping away at that mess by pushing Gemini deeper into the apps where you already spend your day — and into the ones you wish would just talk to each other.

## A louder voice and a custom look in Google Vids

The engine behind AI voiceovers and avatar narration in Google Vids has been upgraded. According to Google's announcement, the text-to-speech system — the part that turns written words into spoken audio — now runs on the Gemini 3.8 Flash Lite TTS model. Google says the result is more natural and expressive narration.

Captions got their own upgrade. Until now, captions in Google Vids came in a single style. You can now change their font and typography, move them around the screen, and adjust how they animate. For anyone making branded training videos, internal explainers, or social clips, that means the captions can finally match the rest of the look without leaving the app.

## "Skills" are replacing Gems in the Gemini app

If you've built saved instructions in the Gemini app or Workspace — what Google used to call Gems — the company is gradually replacing them with something called **skills**. A skill is a reusable prompt, basically a saved set of instructions you can fire off again and again ("summarize this email in three bullets", "rewrite this in a friendlier tone"). Google says skills will roll out to Workspace users over the coming weeks and will eventually take over from Gems entirely. If you already lean on Gems, it's worth keeping an eye out so your saved instructions don't quietly vanish in the switch.

## Connecting Gemini to apps outside Google

Gemini already lives inside Gmail, Calendar, and Drive, but most people's work doesn't stop at Google's door. According to Google's announcement, new Gemini connectors are designed to plug into business tools — like a CRM (a customer relationship management system — think of it as your company's contact and sales tracker), a project management platform, a marketing automation tool, or a help desk. For broader reach, Google points to Zapier as a way to securely extend Gemini's access to other apps in your **tech stack** — Google's term for all the software your team uses day to day. Together, the two paths aim to give Gemini a more complete view of your work, so you spend less time copying and pasting between tabs.

## Smaller updates for builders and security-minded teams

Two quieter announcements round out the week. Developers can now create, read, and manage comments across the Docs, Sheets, and Slides APIs (application programming interfaces — basically the back door that lets other software talk to Google Docs and its siblings). Google Docs also picked up **suggested edits** support through the API, so an automated tool can propose a revision for you to accept or reject instead of changing the document on its own. And there's a new simple setup option for Workspace client-side encryption — the kind of feature IT teams tend to care about when they want tighter control over who can read sensitive files.

## What this means for you

- **If you mostly use Google Workspace for personal tasks:** The video changes are the most visible. Try the upgraded voiceover in Google Vids next time you make a quick explainer, and play with the new caption controls to match the look of your video.
- **If you run a small business or work in a team:** Skills are the one to watch. Save your best prompts as skills now so the transition from Gems is painless. If your team uses tools outside Google, ask your admin whether Gemini connectors are enabled — they could save a lot of tab-switching.
- **If you're just curious about AI:** Nothing here is urgent, but it's a clear signal that Gemini is no longer "an AI in a chat box." It's quietly becoming the layer that ties Google's productivity tools — and a growing list of third-party apps — together.
- **If you already use these tools:** Experiment with combining skills and connectors — for example, a skill that summarizes messages could pull from inside a connected CRM, not just Gmail, once the connectors are live for your account.

## Wrap-up

The big story here isn't a single dramatic feature — it's the direction. Google is turning Gemini from a chatbot into connective tissue across the apps where you already work. A useful next step today: open the Gemini app or Google Vids and try one of the new features, even a small one. That short experiment will tell you which of these updates actually changes your daily flow.
